slides.texte_overlay:
7 low-key habits that make
your words carry weight
Saying less in meetings. One clear contribution beats ten small comments. When you speak rarely and well, people start leaning in the moment you open your mouth.
Never exaggerating. Not "the best ever", not "literally dying". Accurate words build a reputation for honesty, and honest people's words weigh more.
Keeping your promises small and certain. Promise only what you're sure to deliver, then deliver it early. Reliability is what makes your word worth something.
Using a calm, even voice. No rushing, no rising pitch at the end of every sentence. A steady voice signals that you truly believe what you're saying.
Knowing what you're talking about. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and real knowledge gives my opinions a weight they never had before.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Real knowledge gives my opinions a weight they never had before.

slides.texte_overlay: Admitting what you don't know. "Good question, I'm not sure." People trust the man who doesn't bluff, and they believe him much more when he is sure.
Backing your point with one example. Not a lecture, just one clear story or number. A single good example makes an idea stick far better than repetition.
